rl.name: MSA
rl.description: Master Services Agreement. Umbrella contract between a Client and a Supplier governing all future engagements: agreement reference, effective date, initial term, expiry date, governing law, client jurisdiction, number of Statements of Work, total contract value, auto-renewal, payment terms and late interest, limitation of liability cap, indemnity, insurance, confidentiality, termination notice, non-solicitation, SLA credits, data protection and dispute resolution.

rl.name: SOW
rl.description: Statement of Work. Project-specific document issued under and governed by a parent Master Services Agreement (refers to the MSA reference and date). Contains SOW reference, parent agreement, service description, start and end date, duration, commercial model (fixed price or time and materials), SOW value, team size in FTE, scope of services, deliverables and milestones with target dates and percentage of value, charges and payment schedule.

rl.name: NDA
rl.description: Non-Disclosure Agreement. Standalone confidentiality agreement between parties: definition of confidential information, obligations of the receiving party, permitted disclosures, exclusions, term of confidentiality, return or destruction of information, remedies and governing law. No services, deliverables or pricing.

rl.name: EC
rl.description: Employment Contract. Agreement between an employer and an individual employee: job title, date of joining, probation period, salary and benefits, working hours, leave, notice period, termination of employment, non-compete, and employee confidentiality obligations.

THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is made and entered into on 16 June 2022 (the "Effective Date"),
BY AND BETWEEN:
(1) Brightpath Transport S.L., a company incorporated under the laws of the Kingdom of Spain (Commercial Reg. No.
B-226272), having its registered office at Via de Ema Iborra 632 Apt. 40 , Madrid (the "Client"); and
(2) Meridian Global Technologies Inc., a company incorporated in Delaware, USA (Delaware Reg. No. 5541203), having
its principal place of business at 1200 Innovation Parkway, Suite 400, Wilmington, DE 19801, USA (the "Supplier").
The Client and the Supplier are together referred to as the "Parties" and each individually as a "Party".
RECITALS
A. The Client wishes to procure certain information technology, software development and managed services in connection
with its logistics operations.
B. The Supplier is engaged in the business of providing information technology outsourcing, software engineering and
related professional services and has agreed to provide such services to the Client on the terms of this Agreement.
C. This Agreement sets out the framework terms under which the Supplier shall provide services to the Client pursuant to
one or more Statements of Work executed hereunder.
1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
"Statement of Work" or "SOW" means a document executed by the Parties under this Agreement describing specific
services, deliverables, timelines and charges. Each SOW forms part of and is governed by this Agreement.
"Charges" means the fees payable by the Client to the Supplier as set out in the applicable SOW. "Deliverables" means the
outputs to be delivered by the Supplier as specified in a SOW. In the event of conflict between this Agreement and a SOW,
this Agreement shall prevail except where the SOW expressly states otherwise.
2. TERM AND RENEWAL
This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier in accordance with its terms, shall
continue for an initial term of 3 year(s), expiring on 16 June 2025 (the "Initial Term").
Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive periods of 2 year(s) unless either
Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior to the end of the then-current term.
3. SCOPE OF SERVICES
The Supplier shall provide the services described in each SOW (the "Services"). As at the Effective Date, 4 Statement(s) of
Work has/have been agreed, as listed in Schedule 1. Additional SOWs may be executed from time to time and shall be
governed by this Agreement.
4. CHARGES, INVOICING AND PAYMENT
The Client shall pay the Charges set out in each SOW. Unless otherwise stated in a SOW, the Supplier shall invoice
monthly in arrears, and the Client shall pay undisputed invoices within 30 days of the date of a valid invoice (Net 30).
Late payment of undisputed amounts shall accrue interest at 1.5% per month. All Charges are exclusive of applicable taxes,
which shall be borne by the Client.
The aggregate value of the Statements of Work in force as at the Effective Date is €3,312,000.
5. CONFIDENTIALITY
Each Party shall keep confidential all Confidential Information of the other Party and shall not use or disclose it except as
necessary to perform this Agreement. These obligations shall survive termination for a period of 5 years.


CONFIDENTIAL
MSA-001-2022
Page 3
6. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
The Supplier retains ownership of all software, frameworks and accelerators and grants the Client a non-exclusive,
non-transferable licence for internal use for the term of the applicable Statement of Work.
7. DATA PROTECTION
Each Party shall comply with all applicable data-protection laws, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation
(GDPR) and Spanish Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD). Where the Supplier processes personal data on behalf of the
Client, it shall do so only on documented instructions and shall implement appropriate technical and organisational
measures. A separate Data Processing Addendum shall apply where required by law.
8. WARRANTIES
The Supplier warrants that the Services shall be performed with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with good
industry practice, and that Deliverables shall materially conform to the specifications set out in the applicable SOW for a
period of ninety (90) days following acceptance.
9. INDEMNIFICATION
[Mutual indemnity (capped)] Each party shall indemnify the other for third-party claims arising from bodily injury, death,
or damage to tangible property caused by the negligent acts of the indemnifying party, and for intellectual-property
infringement claims.
10. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
Subject to the exclusions below, the total aggregate liability of either Party arising out of or in connection with this
Agreement and any SOW shall not exceed a fixed amount of EUR 920,000 (the "Liability Cap"; cap basis: Fixed monetary
cap).
Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential losses, or for loss of profits, revenue or
anticipated savings. The Liability Cap shall not apply to liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud,
breach of confidentiality, or a Party's indemnification obligations.
11. INSURANCE
The Supplier shall maintain, at its own cost, professional indemnity and cyber-liability insurance with a minimum coverage
of €4,600,000 per claim, and shall provide evidence of such coverage upon reasonable request.
12. SERVICE LEVELS AND SERVICE CREDITS
Service levels applicable to each engagement are set out in the relevant SOW. Where the Supplier fails to meet an agreed
service level, the Client shall be entitled to liquidated damages as set out in the SOW. The aggregate service credits /
liquidated damages payable in any calendar month shall not exceed 10% of the Charges payable for that month for the
affected SOW. Service credits are the Client's sole financial remedy for service-level failures, save for the Client's
termination rights.
13. TERMINATION
Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW for convenience by giving the other Party not less than 90 days'
prior written notice.
Either Party may terminate immediately on written notice if the other Party commits a material breach which is not
remedied within thirty (30) days of notice, or becomes insolvent. On termination, the Client shall pay for Services properly
performed up to the effective date of termination.
14. NON-SOLICITATION
During the term of this Agreement and for 6 months thereafter, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment any
personnel of the other Party who was directly involved in the performance of the Services, save for general public
advertising.


CONFIDENTIAL

Page 4
15. FORCE MAJEURE
Neither Party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance (other than payment obligations) to the extent caused by
events beyond its reasonable control, provided it takes reasonable steps to mitigate the effects.
16. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Kingdom of Spain. The Parties shall
attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute by negotiation. Failing resolution, disputes shall be referred to arbitration under
the Court of Arbitration of Madrid, and the courts of the courts of Madrid, Spain shall have jurisdiction
